agent.name: Emerging Technology Creation Agent — Historical Risk Lens
agent.specialty: Creation and capability lineage with historically grounded implementation red flags

analytical_question: Does historical GPT-2 training-data extraction prove that an unnamed current vendor trains on and leaks client uploads?
general_et_finding: Creation lineage: transformer attention (2017), large-scale pretraining and few-shot task reuse (2020), and human-feedback instruction tuning (2022) combined capabilities addressing efficient language processing, task flexibility and user intent [sources 1–3]. Parallel computation, text corpora and human demonstrations were enabling resources. Inference: reuse across tasks created economic incentives; the source set does not quantify their causal importance. Historical limitations include remaining mistakes despite tuning, demonstrated training-data extraction from GPT-2, and indirect prompt injection in integrated applications [sources 3–5]. These are selective milestones and mechanisms, not proof of present vendor behavior or a forecast of failure. The organization changes exposure and consequences, not this history.
application_finding: No. The cited study supports a historical training-data extraction mechanism in its tested setting. It does not establish whether a current service ingests uploads into training, retains them, exposes them through retrieval or leaks them.
organization_specific_finding: The firm has not supplied a vendor, configuration or data-handling contract. These omissions warrant verification and a bounded evaluation; they are not evidence that a particular vendor leaks information.

evidence.claim: The Transformer combined attention-based sequence modeling with a more parallelizable architecture, demonstrated on translation tasks.
evidence.source_or_reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2017; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Historical architecture evidence; not proof of performance in either hypothetical organization.

evidence.claim: GPT-3 demonstrated task adaptation from text examples without task-specific parameter updates, with uneven results across tasks.
evidence.source_or_reference: Brown et al. (2020), Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2020; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Supports a historical scaling and pretraining milestone; not a current model benchmark.

evidence.claim: InstructGPT combined supervised demonstrations and human-preference reinforcement learning; instruction-following improved but mistakes remained.
evidence.source_or_reference: Ouyang et al. (2022), Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2022; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Supports the distinction between instruction-following and guaranteed correctness.

evidence.claim: Training-data extraction was demonstrated against GPT-2, including some publicly available personal information.
evidence.source_or_reference: Carlini et al. (2020; revised 2021), Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07805
evidence.date_or_recency: Original abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06
evidence.notes: Not proof that a current service trains on customer uploads or leaks them. Scope: GPT-2 experiment.

evidence.claim: Indirect prompt injection was demonstrated in LLM-integrated applications through instructions embedded in retrieved data.
evidence.source_or_reference: Greshake et al. (2023), Not what you have signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12173
evidence.date_or_recency: Original abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06
evidence.notes: Mechanism evidence, not a current vulnerability determination for an unspecified product.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Evidence reviewed consists of five original-paper abstracts and submission histories, not full-paper methods or reproduced experiments.
No current provider, model version or configuration is specified. No current vulnerability, error rate or training-use policy can be concluded.
Synthetic cases and same-assistant evaluation do not establish deployment safety, readiness or measured productivity.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that the cited historical demonstrations were reported; moderate confidence in the inferred exposure pathways; current exploitability and control effectiveness are unknown. Priorities are qualitative, not probability estimates.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential drafting assistance remains plausible if checking effort is manageable. Controls impose work; no net saving is established.
risk_governance_implication: Privacy inference boundary: source 4 -> demonstrated historical extraction -> reason to investigate data pathways. Do not equate historical training-set memorization with retention of inference-time inputs or cross-client retrieval. These are distinct mechanisms requiring separate evidence. Source 5 separately motivates testing untrusted document handling in tool-connected systems. Keep confidential inputs and automatic delivery outside evaluation until accountable reviewers resolve the relevant facts.
recommendation_management_implication: Reject the question’s unsupported conclusion. Request current, product-specific documentation and configuration evidence; refer interpretation and approval to the privacy/security reviewer. Do not invent a provider policy or guarantee of safety.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess when a specific product and current data-handling evidence are supplied.
Reassess if actual incident evidence or configuration tests establish an exposure pathway.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Cannot answer whether this vendor trains on or leaks uploads without identifying the vendor and obtaining relevant evidence.
